$comment: The only sentences any public asset may assert about what this framework does. AGENTS.md: 'every claim in the docs, the ADR, the PR body and the JTBD matrix traces to a merged test — a capability and its limitation are stated in the same breath.' This file extends that rule to marketing. Templates reference claims by id ({{claim:C-01}}); `npm run site:check` fails the build if a claim is missing evidence, missing a limitation, references a file that does not exist, or is defined and never used.

measuredAgainst.note: Re-measure and update this block before any public launch. A claims file measured against a stale SHA is a claims file that lies.

claims.text: Write a module manifest; the agent turns it into a migration, a service, a REST resource, an SDK method and Admin screens — with no page code.
claims.limitation: Generated CRUD only. The factory does not generate workflows or approvals for a custom object — that is still handwritten (JTBD-06, partially supported).

claims.text: Generated objects reference each other: a foreign key, runtime target validation, schema metadata and an Admin selector, all from one field declaration.
claims.limitation: Generated-to-generated many-to-one only. Many-to-many, inverse collections, cascade delete and generated-to-core references do not exist.

claims.text: Commercial policy is deterministic code, not a model's judgement: a renewal at or above the threshold stops and waits for a named human.
claims.limitation: Proven for the built-in renewal object and its single value threshold. A general policy engine over arbitrary custom objects does not exist.

claims.text: The agent cannot approve on the human's behalf. A test asserts the refusal, so the boundary is a property of the system rather than a promise in a README.

evidence.testName: approval workflow rejects an agent pretending to make the human decision

claims.limitation: The actor is asserted, not authenticated: there is no auth, tenancy or RBAC, and an actor header is not identity. This holds a boundary against an honest agent, not against an attacker with network access.

claims.text: Opportunities move through code-first pipeline stages under a server-authoritative action — the client asks, the server decides.
claims.limitation: Pipelines are proven on the built-in Opportunity module. Configurable pipelines for generated custom objects are not claimed.

claims.text: A lead is captured, scored, routed, qualified and converted into Company, Contact and Opportunity through explicit actions, each one atomic and audited.

evidence.jtbd: JTBD-04, JTBD-05, JTBD-05b, JTBD-LI-01, JTBD-LI-02, JTBD-LI-04

claims.limitation: Enrichment runs against a fixture provider — no real external data source is wired. The Lead model is the starter's, not a built-in core module.

claims.text: Scoring is explainable and versioned: every score carries the fingerprint of the model version that produced it, so a number from last quarter can still be accounted for.
claims.limitation: Deterministic weighted rules, not a machine-learning model. Nothing trains, fits or backtests.

claims.text: Quotes price on the server from a catalog — one-time and recurring, flat, per-unit, volume and graduated tiers — and freeze into an immutable version when a discount goes for approval.
claims.limitation: Catalog sync runs against a fixture provider; no real external catalog (Stripe, Zuora, ERP) is connected. Money is integer cents with no FX — currencies are never summed.

claims.text: A signature envelope produces verified events and a hashed signed artifact, and exactly one immutable Order is built from the approved quote version.
claims.limitation: A fixture signature provider with a test-only webhook key. No DocuSign, Adobe Sign or Dropbox Sign adapter exists, and the artifact hash is provider-reported rather than independently recomputed.

claims.text: A signed Order activates into a Commercial Contract, an immutable contract version, a Subscription and explicitly pending delivery and service obligations — every component classified, never guessed.
claims.limitation: The term is post-signature operational metadata, not a signed contractual term. Nothing bills, renews, amends or cancels: there is no scheduler, so auto-renew and notice periods are recorded and never fire.

claims.text: Pending obligations hand over into a Delivery Project with work packages, milestones and an optional partner — atomically, idempotently, and across a package boundary the kernel never learns about.
claims.limitation: It hands work over and runs it through human-driven transitions. Nothing schedules, staffs, computes percent complete, accepts or bills. Deliverables and customer acceptance do not exist as objects.

claims.text: Delivery records what it consumed: append-only time and expense evidence, costed server-side by a versioned fingerprinted policy, with a reproducible contribution estimate grouped by currency.
claims.limitation: Deliberately not a margin: no revenue recognition, no cost of goods sold, no ARR/MRR/TCV, no annualization, no FX. A project carrying a recurring obligation returns no estimate at all and says why.

claims.text: A customer-authored domain package attaches and detaches with the kernel's fingerprint unchanged, and reaches another package only through a capability it declares.
claims.limitation: No scaffold, no registry, no marketplace, and no sandboxing — package code runs with the host process's authority. Detaching leaves its data behind; there is no uninstall.

claims.text: One command tells an agent what an application actually is — packages, capabilities, resources, actions, policies, providers — read from checked-in source, in a single deterministic JSON report.
claims.limitation: Source-only and read-only. It never opens the database, contacts a provider, reads a secret, or reports runtime, CI or authorization state — and it lists those blind spots as machine-readable limitations in its own output.

claims.text: One command composes the whole thing and then inspects it: 61 modules, 3 packages, 25 resources, 42 actions, 5 policies and 10 providers, applied from manifests and driven end to end — then it prints the eleven things the inspector says it cannot see.

repoFacts: npm run tour runs examples/starters/b2b-lead-qualification/install.mjs, which CI runs on every push, into a directory it keeps
the counts are the app inspect report of that composed project
scripts/tour.js exits non-zero if the composed application is ever empty

claims.limitation: It composes the starter's application, not yours, and it runs entirely locally against SQLite with no authentication. The counts describe what that starter applies; a different composition gives different numbers. Wall-clock time varies by machine and is deliberately not claimed.

claims.text: The same refusal holds where the money is: an agent actor asking to approve a discounted quote is refused with a 403, and only a human user actor can decide.

evidence.testName: commercial e2e: approval boundary, revise/version-2, concurrency, fault injection, provider failures, drift
evidence.assertion: tests/commercial-e2e.test.js — quote.approve with actor { type: 'agent' } rejects with status 403 and code HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED

claims.limitation: The assertion lives inside a composite end-to-end test rather than a test named for it, so the citation is a file and a line rather than a test name. Extracting it into a named test is tracked in docs/strategy/GO_TO_MARKET.md; until then, cite the line.

claims.text: A Solution Plan is a checked-in file with a contract and a canonical fingerprint, validated against a real inspection — so a plan written against a composition that has since moved reports itself stale.
claims.limitation: A document contract, not a planner and not a runtime. Nothing executes a plan, and the validator refuses a plan that carries a command.

claims.text: Every mutation goes through a module service or a named workflow, and leaves an audit event and a step-level trace behind it.
claims.limitation: Audit records what the process did under an asserted actor. It is not a tamper-evident or externally attestable log, and it is not a compliance control.

claims.text: Zero third-party runtime dependencies. Node 22 and a checkout — no build step, no bundler, no framework underneath your framework.

repoFacts: the HTTP server, test runner and database adapter are all Node built-ins

claims.limitation: Development dependencies and the eventual PostgreSQL adapter are separate questions. Having no runtime dependencies is a property of the framework, not of whatever you add on top of it.

claims.text: The MCP server exposes project context and narrow write tools to a coding agent; anything that generates code or destroys state is dry-run unless you pass an explicit apply flag.
claims.limitation: Stdio only, local only. There is no hosted or authenticated MCP endpoint, and the server inherits the local process's authority.

claims.text: Generated modules evolve without rewriting history: explicit revisions, a checked-in state file and append-only named migrations.
claims.limitation: The view is source-only: what the checked-in revisions and migrations say is knowable; what a particular database has actually applied is not.

claims.text: 497 tests, run on every push, covering happy paths and the policy boundaries that matter — hostile input, transaction rollback, idempotency, concurrency and immutability among them.

repoFacts: npm run verify at 345c809: 497 passing, 0 failing
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs verify and smoke on push and pull_request

claims.limitation: A test count measures effort, not correctness — read the adversarial-review categories in docs/QUALITY_GATES.md to see what is actually attacked. Real-browser tests are run manually and are not in CI.

claims.text: Five rules can be removed on purpose in one command, and the suite catches every one in about two seconds — naming the test that caught it. Anything that survives is reported as a gap, not omitted.

repoFacts: npm run falsify at 345c809: 5 caught, 0 survived, 0 stale, 2.2s
npm run falsify --only delivery-cost-rounding: caught by 'cost arithmetic is exact at every boundary' in 108.3s
the run refuses to start over uncommitted target files and verifies every restore byte-for-byte

claims.limitation: It falsifies six named rules, not the twenty-two claims in this ledger, and it proves only that a test holds each one — a rule that is wrong but faithfully defended passes every mutation. It is not mutation testing: nothing is generated or sampled, and no score is derived.

limitations.headline: No authentication, tenancy or RBAC.
limitations.text: The server is local-development-only. An actor header is an assertion, not an identity. Do not expose it to a network.

repoFacts: crm app inspect reports productionPosture: local development only

limitations.headline: SQLite only.
limitations.text: Persistence is Node's built-in SQLite adapter. PostgreSQL is on the Production Spine track and is not implemented.

limitations.headline: The build benchmark has not been run.
limitations.text: The protocol is designed and published; no Successful Agent Build Rate exists yet. Any number you see quoted for this project is not ours.

limitations.headline: No scheduler, no task engine, no reminders.
limitations.text: One follow-up Task is created inside lead qualification. There is no recurring work, no delayed workflow, no queue — so nothing fires on a renewal notice period either.

limitations.headline: No email, calendar or marketing integrations.
limitations.text: An in-memory notification provider contract exists. No adapter sends anything to anyone.

limitations.headline: No import, export, dedupe, merge, bulk edit, saved views or global search.
limitations.text: Table stakes in every commercial CRM, and none of them has a milestone yet. This is recorded deliberately rather than left for you to discover.

limitations.headline: Ownership today means copying source, not installing a dependency.
limitations.text: There is no create-project CLI and no published package. The one working installer copies packages/, apps/ and examples/ into a new project — you own the result outright, but the ergonomics of `npm create` and a versioned framework dependency do not exist yet. Until they do, upgrading means merging, not bumping.

repoFacts: examples/starters/b2b-lead-qualification/install.mjs copies packages, apps, examples and package.json into a temporary project
the create-project CLI is EXECUTION_ROADMAP Phase 5 and is not implemented

limitations.headline: You cannot put real customer data in this yet.
limitations.text: A CRM is a personal-data system by definition, and this one has no authentication, no tenancy, no export and no erasure path — so there is no way to service a data-subject access or deletion request with it. Data governance is designed and unimplemented. The one thing that does hold today: lead scoring is deterministic, versioned and explainable, not a model's judgement about a person.

repoFacts: DATA_GOVERNANCE.md records the whole track as design only
scoring is a deterministic weighted model with a persisted version fingerprint (C-07)

limitations.headline: This is a framework, not a product you sign up for.
limitations.text: There is no hosted CRM, no free tier and no account. The output is an application in your repository that you run.
